readme.text: [](#测试) [](LICENSE) **简体中文** | [English](README.en.md) > **AI 使用说明** —— 本项目由 AI 助手协助整理撰写：源码、测试、文档与提交信息均由 AI 智能体（DSH Agent，运行于 DeepSeek Harness）在人类指导下起草；需求定义、方案决策与最终验收由人类作者完成。
检测并提前中断 [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 中的**推理复读**——「思维链循环卡死」：模型其实已经想完了，却卡在「准备输出」上无限打转，白烧掉几分钟和几十万字符，直到用户放弃并按下停止。它把「静默卡死好几分钟」变成「立刻可见的报错」。

在一次被完整记录的会话里（12 轮、324 步），**12 轮中有 11 轮**以完全相同的方式结束：模型**早已做完真正的工程工作**——看截图、算坐标、决定改哪个脚本——然后卡在「准备输出」阶段，反复催促自己却始终不落笔（`Let me write. Go. OK. Emit. Now.`）。单步输出 **24–28 万字符**、耗时 **208 秒**，直到用户按下停止。这 11 条 assistant 消息的 `stopReason` 都是**空字符串**，内容只有**一个 `reasoning` 块**——没有 `text`，也没有 `tool-call`：模型没产出任何可执行动作，只是在思考里空转。而 DSH 当时没有任何护栏能发现并提前叫停。

**做法。** 插件挂在 `llm/stream` 瀑布钩子上（正是 DSH 自己的 `llm-invariant` 所用的同一个扩展点），**只测量流式推理文本**，每 200 字符在滚动缓冲区上评估五条判据；命中即**停止向上游拉取**，并发出终止块：

```js
{ type: "finish", reason: { kind: "error", failure: { message, code: "REASONING_LOOP_GUARD" } } }
```

DSH 随后走它既有的 provider 错误路径：本步以一个可见错误结束，而不是静默空转。**效果**：记录在案的 11 次真实故障**全部在 10,000 字符以内被拦住**；在本机 2,799 条真实推理流（1,920 万字符）上只触发 7 次，且**全部是真循环**。

| 判据 | 定义 | 实测峰值（11 正 / 166 负） | 阈值 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `periodic-run`（主判据） | 缓冲区尾部存在 ≥ `minUnits` 个**连续相同的单元**，周期 p ∈ [8, 400]；单元本身是更短串的重复（`xxxx…`、`abab…`）时不算 | 正 **0..8**，负 **0..2** | 4 |
| `block-repeat` | 同一 `blockMin` 字符的块在窗口内出现 ≥ `blockCount` 次，**且相邻两次的间距全部相等** | 正 **0..2**，负 **0..0** | 4 |
| `line-repeat` | 同一**散文**行（≥ `lineMin` 字符）出现 ≥ `lineCount` 次，**且**占窗口比例 ≥ `lineShare`；代码 / 标记 / diff 行被测量但从不被报告 | 正 **2..2**，负 **0..0** | 3 + 10% |
| `kgram-repeat` | 末尾 `kgram` 个字符在窗口内出现 ≥ `kgramThreshold` 次 | 正 **1..5**，负 **1..1** | 12 |
| `filler-run`（兜底） | **原始**文本末尾连续 ≥ `fillerRun` 个装饰字符（空白 / 标点 / 符号） | 见下文「装饰不是复读」 | 400 |

五条判据是**析取**的：正样本不必触发某一条特定的判据，只要够到任意一条阈值即可。记录在案的 11 次故障里，**2 次由 `periodic-run` 拦下、9 次由 `line-repeat` 拦下**；负样本的最佳比值只到 **0.50**，正样本最低 **1.00**，分离点在 1.00。**只测量 `reasoning-delta`，绝不测量 `block-end`**——后者会重放整个块的文本，等于人为制造出它正要寻找的那种重复。**也绝不测量 `text-delta`**：正常的长输出（表格、代码）本来就可能重复，漏报好过误杀。

> **一条窗口内的共现不是复读。** 上面三条计数判据最初只看「窗口里出现了几次」。一次真实会话里因此连续迎来 5 次误报，全是这个错误：模型在推理里反复引用同一行 Java 语句、几条并列的 `runcode` 命令共享同一段前缀、以及它真在逐字打出 36 个 `x` 的图块。真正的复读是**时间里**的重复——等距推进，或一直延续到尾部。判别量因此分成几层，见下文。

readme.section: 为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件
readme.text:
**同一行出现两次就判循环**在写代码、写文档时是常态——重构时同一个标识符落在两行，写 changelog 时写了两遍 `## Unreleased`。这个问题**没能在 177 样本定标集上暴露**，因为那 11 正 + 166 负**全是散文**，根本不含「边写代码边推理」这一整个失败形态：在那个形态上，0/166 误报说明不了任何事。

真正的定标改在**本机 2,799 条真实推理流**（1,920 万字符，含 11 个已知真循环）上做。旧默认在该语料上触发 **180 次**（`line-repeat` 177、`block-repeat` 3），新默认下只剩 **7 次且全部是真循环**：

readme.section: 为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件
readme.text:
- **count 单独不够。** 语料里最常见的口头禅 `Let me write.` 最高能到 17 次，而最弱的真循环是 29 次，只有 1.7 倍余量，不足以押上「打断用户」的代价。
- **share 是判别量。** 重复行占窗口的比例：健康流最高 **6.1%**，最弱真循环 **10.2%**。取 8% 会放进两条误报，取 12% 会漏掉真循环，所以默认 10%。
- **count 也不能退回 2。** 一条 72 字符的长**散文**行只出现 **2 次**就能把 share 顶到 **18.7%**，光靠 share 地板拦不住它。（这个论证原文用的是 41 字符长标识符，但标识符如今已被下面的第三条排除，故改用散文行。）
- **`block-repeat` 只需把 `blockCount` 从 3 提到 4**：3 会在健康推理**引用长文本**时触发（十六进制 dump、插件名清单、系统提示词复述），4 在语料上只剩 3 次触发且全为真循环。这里刻意**不加** share 地板——从 0% 到 25% 结果都一样，加了只是没有数据支撑的复杂度。

readme.section: 为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件
readme.text:
**第三条：被报告的行必须不是代码。** 归一化剥掉空白、标点与符号，而这恰好是区分两行代码的全部信息。一次真实误报：801 字符的推理片段里有五行

```
if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {                    （普通引用，出现三次）
-                if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {   （diff 的删除行）
+                if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {   （diff 的新增行）
```

全部归一化成 `ifeisKeyboardEvent`，于是「同一行出现 5 次、占窗口 22.6%」，两条地板同时越过。而模型并没有循环——它在推理一处代码改动，下一个尝试是 4,084 字符的普通工作、一条判据都不触发。这个触发点又恰好落在 `minChars` 大小的第一个判定窗口里，那里几个重复已经占了很大比例。

readme.section: 为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件
readme.text:
**任何阈值都够不着它**：`lineCount` 要从 3 提到 6 才能挡下这一次，而 6 已在真循环占据的区间内；把 `lineShare` 抬过去则会牺牲夹具里的真实检测。所以规则改为**不报告** `CODE_LINE` 认定为代码、标记或 diff 行的行，但**仍把它们计入分母**（只从分母里也删掉会反过来抬高代码密集流的占比，是同一个错误的镜像）。

| 候选做法 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 抬高 `lineCount` / `lineShare` | 要么漏检，要么只是把门槛挪到别处 |
| 归一化前先剥 diff 标记 | **无效**——`STRIP` 本来就剥 `-` / `+` 与空白，剥与不剥结果相同 |
| 干脆去掉归一化 | **无效**——同一片段仍达 `count=3 · share=11.3%`，照常触发 |
| **按行的种类排除**（采用） | 误报消失，且是**分类**排除、不是抬阈值 |

readme.section: 为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件
readme.text:
在**本机 3,862 条真实推理流**上复核：这条修复去掉该次误报与另一条同形态误报（从 HTML 里引用的 `

` 出现三次），其余**零变化**——夹具仍是 166 健康 0 误报 / 11 退化全命中，语料里两条 `line-repeat` 触发仍是同样的真循环（`count` 30 与 19，未变）。标记集刻意取窄：花括号、标记语言标签、行首 diff 标记，这些都不会出现在普通散文里；而更宽的做法（排除任何括号或运算符）会连 `The config (see above) is wrong.` 一起压制，等于让规则对真实的散文口头禅失明。 顺带修掉一个语义缺陷：`line-repeat` / `block-repeat` 原来在第一个达标的单元上就返回，所以日志里的 `count` 永远等于阈值本身，从未反映真实重复次数。现在都改为全扫描取最大重复单元，`count` 因此是真实值。

readme.section: 一次窗口不是一个循环：第二层判别
readme.text:
| 现场 | 旧判据看到的 | 实际发生的事 | 修法 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 推理里四次引用同一行 Java 语句 `StarSystemAPI sys = (StarSystemAPI)Global…getContainingLocation();` | `line-repeat`：`count=4`、`share=10.2%`，刚过两条地板 | 四条引用散布在整个窗口里，间距 **424 / 602 / 259**，毫无节律 | 把该行认成代码——`CODE_LINE` 加上**行尾分号**与**点号调用链** |
| 四条并列的 `runcode` 命令（加行星 / 加小行星带 / 加星云 / 加行星环）共享读当前星系的前缀 | `block-repeat`：同一 100 字符块出现 4 次 | 间距 **1130 / 359 / 742**，是并列命令而非复读 | 要求重复块**等距出现**（`count` 改报最长等距链长，原始次数留在 `rawCount`） |
| 模型在写 6×6 图块的字面量 `"xxxxxxxx…"` | `periodic-run`：`units=4`、`period=8` | 单元 `xxxxxxxx` 本身就是**同一个字符的重复**——它在打字，不是在循环 | 单元是更短串的整数次重复时直接否决（`isRepeatedUnit`） |

readme.section: 一次窗口不是一个循环：第二层判别
readme.text:
三条都是**分类判断**，不是抬阈值。抬阈值已经被实测排除：`lineCount` 要从 3 提到 6 才挡得住第一例，而 6 已在真循环占据的区间内。

复核口径：在同一批语料上（chunk 7 / 41 / 200 三档各跑一遍），三处修改前后的**触发集合逐字节相同**（`count` 29 / 19 的两条 `line-repeat`、`periodic-run` 的两条），夹具仍是 166 健康 0 误报 / 11 退化全命中，而五条误报全部转为 inert。

前四条判据都在**归一化文本**上计数：先把空白、标点、符号剥掉，再数重复。这一步不是美化，而是修一个真实的误报——最初的实现直接在原始文本上跑周期判据，于是模型画一条 `________` 分隔线就成了「8 个字符重复 6 次」，护栏真的中断了那次流。

清洗类是 `[\s\p{P}\p{S}]`。它是原先那份手写字符表的**严格超集**：`_` 属于 `\p{Pc}`，`─` / `▁` 属于 `\p{So}`，旧表都漏掉了。在全部 11 个真实退化样本上，新旧两类产出的文本**逐字节相同**——加宽只删掉了装饰，没有删掉任何一个真实循环赖以成立的字符。

readme.section: 装饰不是复读，但「一直在画装饰」是
readme.text:
归一化带来一个代价：一个**只**输出装饰的流，在四条计数判据眼里永远是空的。`filler-run` 就是为这一种情况存在的兜底，并且刻意做得很迟钝：

- **它锚定在文本末尾。** 模型完全可以合法地画一张宽表格或 ASCII 图；一旦它接着写散文，那段装饰就不再位于尾部、不再计数。只有**持续**输出装饰的流才会触发——扫全窗口会在模型早已画完的图上误报。
- **门槛远高于任何合法排版。** 实测合法形状的最长装饰段：150 宽的 ASCII 框 **151** 字符、20 列 markdown 表行 **142**、setext 下划线 **62**、`---` 分隔线 **5**。默认值 400 是实测最宽合法形状的 2.6 倍，真正卡住的流会在一个 `every` 周期内越过它。

在六种喂入粒度下（chunk = 1 / 8 / 40 / 200 / 1000 / 4000），五条判据合计仍为 **11/11 全部命中、0/166 零误报**。

本包尚未发布到 npm，从 GitHub 源码安装。DSH 按 profile 隔离：**桌面版用 `desktop`，网页版用 `web`**，装进哪个 profile 就只在那个形态下生效。

```powershell

readme.section: 且要先启动一次 Desktop 初始化它的 profile、完全退出应用，再执行
readme.text: dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:himi-li/dsh-reasoning-loop-guard

readme.section: 网页版：任意 dsh CLI 均可；web profile 不存在时会从随附模板自动创建并初始化
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:himi-li/dsh-reasoning-loop-guard
```

**两种形态的命令只差一个名字。** 通用格式是 `dsh plugin --profile <name> add <包名>`：`web`、`headless`、`sdk`、`sdk-minimal`、`acp` 首次使用时会从随附模板自动初始化，只有 `desktop` 需要「先启动一次、再完全退出」。同一个包可以分别装进多个 profile，互不影响。卸载用 `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-reasoning-loop-guard`。

readme.section: 网页版：任意 dsh CLI 均可；web profile 不存在时会从随附模板自动创建并初始化
readme.text: 这条命令把包装进 profile 的 `dependencies`，并自动把声明了 `dsh.bundle` 的包追加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`——两处都会写，不需要手改 `package.json`。**本包不需要 `allowBuilds` 授权。** 从 git 安装的插件通常要跑 `prepare` 构建脚本，而 pnpm ≥10 默认拒绝，用户得先往 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里写 `allowBuilds` 再重试；本包直接分发构建好的纯 JavaScript（`lib/` 已入库），没有 `prepare` 脚本，首次 `add` 即可装成。

readme.section: 网页版：任意 dsh CLI 均可；web profile 不存在时会从随附模板自动创建并初始化
readme.text: 不想用 `dsh plugin` 的话，也可以自己在 profile 的 `package.json` 里写 `dependencies`（配 `pnpm install`）和 `dsh.profile.bundles` 两处，或者在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里直接挂载（本包自带的 `cordis.patch.yml` 就是这一份）。**`dependencies` 和 `bundles` 两处都要写**：插件页只列出存在于 `dependencies` 里的包，而 `bundles` 决定它是否被装载。

readme.section: 网页版：任意 dsh CLI 均可；web profile 不存在时会从随附模板自动创建并初始化
readme.text: **改完需要重启 DSH，而不是只刷新页面。** 两个独立原因：① 宿主对 `node_modules` 的 HMR 是**关闭**的（`dsh-hmr` 的 `ignored` 默认含 `**/node_modules`），包内文件变动不会被监听；② Node 的 ESM 解析器在进程内**永久缓存**每个包的 `exports` 映射，本包新增 `locale/*.json` 这类 export 之后，**同一个宿主进程里永远解析不到它们**——表现为插件页上的标题一直是英文包名，而图标（直读文件、不走 exports）却正常。

readme.section: 网页版：任意 dsh CLI 均可；web profile 不存在时会从随附模板自动创建并初始化
readme.text:
> **给包作者**：不启动 DSH 也能确认元数据读得对（`icon` / `locale` 是否生效）——

| `stripHistory.enabled` | `fa
`validateConfig()` 会拒绝那些**会静默失效**的配置——`kgram > window`、`minPeriod >= maxPeriod`、`periodTail < 2 * maxPeriod`、`failureCode` 为空、`every` 非正数等等——并在报错信息里点名字段。

上表里的 `enabled`、`settingsPath` 与其余开关的七个字段也可以在 **GUI 里改**——`settingsPath` 例外，它只在 patch 里设，GUI 只读显示。在插件页打开本插件，详情页的「触发日志」面板下方有六个区块：**循环守卫**（检测核心）、**自动恢复**、**降低思考强度**、**剥离历史思维链**、**中断时提示**，以及只读的**配置文件**路径。改完点保存，值写进 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-reasoning-loop-guard/config.json`。

**检测核心与中断提示默认开启，三个可选臂默认关闭。** 核心开关是插件本身；提示开关只往屏幕上弹一条提示、不改变任何发给 provider 的内容，所以也默认开着。三条臂都改变了护栏之外的行为，默认取保守的一侧。**关掉检测核心，三条臂随之失效**：它们只可能响应守卫自己抛出的失败，而守卫不再观察任何流之后就不会再抛出这种失败。

**核心开关与 patch 里的同名键不是一回事，但不会互相打架。** patch 里的 `enabled: false` 表示「整插件不注册任何钩子」，只在装载时读一次；设置文件里的 `enabled` 由流监听器**逐请求**读取。判定写成「**显式 `false` 才算关**」：键缺失表示「按出厂设置」，也就是开着——这样旧的 `config.json` 不会被误读成关闭。**保存后不需要重启**：`config.json` 逐键覆盖 patch 配置，每次读取都重新折叠，下一次请求就生效。写入是原子的（临时文件 + rename），读侧对缺失或损坏的 `config.json` 一律回落到基线，**绝不抛异常**——一个写坏的设置文件最多让开关回到默认值，不会让护栏变成 inactive。**GUI 只能写这八个键，检测阈值永远留在 patch 里**，这样「这次触发的阈值到底来自哪个文件」不会变成一个需要猜的问题。

四个开关各自的机制与代价：

- **自动恢复**（`recovery.*`）。守卫中断一次流之后，向会话追加一条纠正消息并重跑同一步。**为什么必须先追加消息**：重试会重发**完全相同的请求**（`buildRequest` 从会话日志重新推导，被中断的 `assistant/attempt` 不参与推导），所以不带新消息的裸重试必然复现同一个循环。重试预算按**步**计（`sessionId:turn:step`）——按会话计会让一轮坏掉就永久禁用，按 attempt 计会让 `maxRetries` 失去意义。这条消息带的是**产出方自己的 `source.kind`**（会话格式 v4 拒绝 `kind: "plugin"`），副作用是 chat UI 会把它渲染成上下文注记而不是用户气泡。本臂的任何内部故障都落到 `next()`，失败保持与没有插件时一样终局。
- **降低思考强度**（`effort.*`）。按档位回写请求的 `reasoningEffort`。这是**针对病因**的一臂——复读是推理档位太高时的症状，护栏本身只缓解症状——所以如果你的 provider 支持更低的档位，这一臂比护栏更根本。它必须跑在 `dsh-agent` 自己的 `agent/request` 监听器之外（核心会重新推导 provider / model / `reasoningEffort` 并丢掉我们设的值），因此用 `{ prepend: true }` 注册并在 `next()` 之后回写。
- **中断时提示**（`notify.enabled`）。每次守卫中断一条流，在窗口角落弹一条 `Toast`，说明是哪条判据、以及它的测量值。它**不改变任何发给 provider 的东西**，也不改变纠正消息的发送者或内容——只是把「刚刚发生过一次中断」这件事说出来。宿主侧新增一条 SSE 路由 `GET /reasoning-loop-guard/events`（走的是与日志路由同一道同源回环栅栏，被拒时同样 403），触发时推一帧 `{"type":"fire","record":…}`；web 半开一个 `EventSource` 订阅它。**为什么不是轮询日志**：要么间隔短到每秒一个请求，要么延迟久到用户会把这次中断归到别处；**为什么通道不是日志**：日志关掉或写失败时提示照样要发——日志是事后记录，这是实时信号。开关**每次触发时重新读取**，所以页面开着不动，改设置也立刻生效。
- **剥离历史思维链**（`stripHistory.enabled`）。DeepSeek 适配器会把历史 assistant 消息的 `reasoning` 作为线上 `thinking` 块回传，于是第 n 轮模型会读到 1..n-1 轮自己的思维链（包括开启循环的那句「让我再验证一遍」

在 DSH 的**插件**页打开本插件，详情页里会多出一个「触发日志」面板：最近的触发记录（时间、判据、模型、已读字符数、肇事尾巴预览）、按判据与按模型的汇总、一键清空，以及日志路径的复制按钮；没有记录时显示明确的空态文案。列表一次取一页、**最多 100 条**，最新在前，最新一条默认展开；工具栏有**全部展开 / 全部收起**（逐条详情）与**收起列表 / 展开列表**（整个列表连同行头），两级折叠各管一层、互不覆盖。

与护栏同源的两半都在本包内：

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [`lib/log-route.js`](lib/log-route.js) | 向宿主的 `webServer` 注册 `GET /reasoning-loop-guard/log`，返回 `{ path, enabled, version, settings, stats, total, matched, entries }`；支持 `limit` / `rule` / `sessionId` / `since` 查询，`POST` 只接受 `{"action":"clear"}` 与 `{"action":"set","patch":{…}}` 两个显式变更（都是破坏性的，**刻意不能由链接或预取触发**）。 |
| [`lib/events.js`](lib/events.js) | 进程内的触发广播 + `GET /reasoning-loop-guard/events` 的 SSE 端点，供角落那条提示订阅。订阅者抛异常只摘掉它自己；路由被销毁时一并断开它持有的连接。 |
| [`lib/client.js`](lib/client.js) | 手写的惰性 CJS bundle（**零构建步骤**），以包名为键注册 `plugins.bundle.config` 槽位并渲染卡片，另在 `shell.overlay` 槽位挂一个只在触发时出现的 `Toast`；运行时只向平台种子表 `require` 两个词：`react` 与 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`。 |

**两条路由都自带同源栅栏。** 宿主的 `webServer` 不提供任何鉴权，所以这道栅栏由插件自己写：非回环 `Host`、`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`、或与 `Host` 不同源的 `Origin`，一律 `403`；日志路由的请求体上限 16 KiB（超出回 `413` 并断开），非 `GET`/`POST` 回 `405`；事件路由只接受 `GET`/`HEAD`。

> 若你的宿主根本没提供 `webServer` 服务，`ctx.inject(["webServer"], …)` 会**静默跳过**两条路由的注册，护栏本体照常工作。这是刻意的：一个诊断面板与一条提示都不该让护栏变成 inactive。

护栏每触发一次，就向 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-reasoning-loop-guard/fires.jsonl` 追加一行 JSON：

```json
{"v":1,"at":1760000000000,"iso":"2026-10-06T15:20:00.000Z","rule":"periodic-run",
 "atChars":3120,"failureCode":"REASONING_LOOP_GUARD","pluginVersion":"0.2.0",
 "sessionId":"...","provider":"...","model":"...","purpose":"...",
 "reasoningEffort":"max","turn":17,"step":2,"attemptId":"...","cwd":"...",

未知字段会直接省略，因此旧记录只是字段更少，不会写成 `null`。几个值得留意的：`ttftMs` 把「模型很慢、然后才开始打转」和「从第一个 token 就在打转」分开；`aborted` 记录判定落地前调用方是否已经放弃；`thresholds` 是产生这次判定的**确切配置**——几个月后要复盘一次误报，靠的就是它；`previewRaw` 只在 `preview` 被截断时出现。**`iso` 存 UTC，界面一律显示本地时间**：落盘的 `iso` 是规范的 UTC 形式（因为它必须无歧义），而面板的行时间与「时间跨度」、`reasoning_loop_log` 的 `list` 行与 `stats` 的 `span:` 行都经同一个 `localStamp()` 渲染，`stats` 的「按天」也按**本地日**切分。

日志是有界的（`journalMaxBytes`，默认 512 KiB → 轮转为 `fires.jsonl.1`），每次写入都包在 try/catch 里，日志故障**只会告警，绝不影响流**。设为 `journal: false` 可整体关闭。插件还会注册一个只读的维护工具 `reasoning_loop_log`：

| `action` | 返回 |
| --- | --- |
| `list`（默认） | 最近的触发记录，最新在前。可按 `rule`、`sessionId`、`since`（epoch 毫秒）过滤，用 `limit` 限制条数。 |
| `stats` | 汇总：总数、按判据、按模型、按天，以及最早/最晚时间戳。 |
| `path` | 解析后的日志路径。 |
| `clear` | 删除日志（连同轮转出的 `.1`）。 |

于是「最近到底有没有在触发、是在哪个模型上触发的？」只需一次工具调用，而不用去会话日志里翻。

**`failureCode` 故意放在默认可重试集合之外。** 可重试的失败码是 `EMPTY_RESPONSE / RATE_LIMIT / SERVER / TIMEOUT / TRANSPORT`，`REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` 不在其中，因此 `dsh-llm-retry` 不会自动重试。原因是：复读是**这次请求本身**的性质，自动重试会把整个 prompt 再发一遍，白烧同样的 token 再复读一次。如果你确实想要重试，把 `failureCode` 设为 `EMPTY_RESPONSE`。

**`failureCode` 默认带命名空间，是为了不和别的插件串台。** 0.2.0 之前默认值是通用的 `REASONING_LOOP`，而**其他插件也会自带循环检测，并按失败码驱动自己的恢复逻辑**。本机实测到的真实冲突：`dsh-our-free-model` v2.0.0 在 `vendor/channel-pack/pack.js` 里编进了自己的 `loop-recovery`，用 `error.code === "REASONING_LOOP"` 精确匹配决定是否**自动续跑**——于是本守卫的中断被它当成自己的失败捕获，随即用 `agent.followup()` 注入一条 `source.kind: "user"` 的消息重排了一整轮。后果有两个且都很难查：**①** 本插件的三个功能开关全关时，看起来仍然「自动触发了」——因为续跑根本不来自本插件；**②** 用户点停止按钮也停不下来——按钮只中止当前流，那条已经排队的续跑消息照样会跑起来。改成 `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` 后精确匹配不再命中。**这类串扰无法从原理上根除**：命名空间只挡住了精确匹配通用码的逻辑，若某个插件改成前缀匹配、或也去认 `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD`，冲突会回来——那时只能把 `failureCode` 改到一个双方都不认的值。反向也要注意：**别的插件自己检测到的循环仍会走它自己的恢复路径**，本插件的开关管不到它。

**应急止血：环境变量。** 又遇到「开关全关却自动续跑、停止按钮也停不下来」时，可以先用环境变量把第三方那一侧关掉，不必等本插件发新版：

| 环境变量 | 设为 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSH_REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` | `0` | 关掉第三方插件**自带的**循环检测。 |
| `DSH_REASONING_LOOP_AUTO_RESUME` | `0` | 关掉第三方插件的**自动续跑**。 |

两个变量都在第三方插件里以「**未设即开**」的方式读取（只在值为 `0` / `false` / `no` / `off` 时判为关），所以必须显式设成 `0`。**它们只影响那个插件自己的行为，不影响本守卫**——本插件不读任何 `DSH_*` 环境变量。设成**系统/用户环境变量**，不要写进 `~/.dsh/.env`（DSH 的启动器把 `DSH_` 前缀列为「只允许启动环境设置」的保留前缀，写在 `.env` 里会被直接拒绝）：

```powershell

**对工具服务没有硬依赖。** 工具是通过 `ctx.inject(["tools"], …)` 注册的——一种**可选**注入。若写成硬 `inject`，那么在任何没有 tools 服务的宿主上插件都会变成 inactive，等于为了一个诊断功能而把护栏本身也关掉了。

两个 smoke 套件通过 [`test/smoke/resolve-hook.mjs`](test/smoke/resolve-hook.mjs) 把 `@deepseek-ai/*` 解析到 app 与 profile 的安装位置，因此不必启动 DSH 就能验证宿主侧的那一半。

开发期间护栏还额外用**真实的 `dsh` CLI 驱动一个真实的 agent loop**做过端到端验证（隔离 profile，默认模型是一个只用于测试的适配器，回放一段退化推理流），两臂十一项断言：护栏开启时退出码 **1**、上游只发出 **3120 / 7659 字符**、stderr 是 `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD: …`；护栏关闭时同一条流退出码 **0**、**7659 / 7659 字符**完整跑完、stdout 输出 `TG-FAKE-OK`。也就是说护栏**确实把上游生成器截断了**，而关掉后同一流毫发无损——排除了「测试装置本身是坏的」。这套端到端装置属于开发脚手架，不随包发布。

护栏的阈值是针对一次真实故障定标的，但那段会话的推理文本属于隐私，因此仓库里提交的 [`test/fixtures/`](test/fixtures/) 夹具是**合成的**。它们复现了原始数据**实测出来的形状**——相同的行数（11 / 166）、相同的逐行字符数（从一条 24.4 万字符的大块，到 502 字符的小块），以及相同的复读几何。生成器带随机种子且完全确定，因此重新生成会产出逐字节相同的文件，任何 diff 都是真实变更。

- **它不是通用看门狗。** 这几条判据针对的是一种特定的退化形态——尾部连续重复。换一种卡法（无限工具调用循环，或模型在语义上绕圈但并不逐字重复）不会触发它。
- **首次触发的位置**取决于喂入粒度：最早约 3000 字符，最晚约 56000 字符。记录在案的 11 次故障都会在 10,000 字符以内被拦住。
- **定标样本曾是单个会话的 177 条，样本量偏小——已知有盲区。** 它全是散文，不含「边写代码边推理」这一形态，因此在那上面报出的 0/166 误报**不能**外推；`line-repeat` / `block-repeat` 的阈值后来改用数千条真实语料重新定标（见「为什么 `line-repeat` 要三个条件」）。若实践中仍出现误报，优先调高 `lineShare`（比例地板）或 `minUnits` / `kgramThreshold`；若误报来自装饰（比如你的模型习惯画很宽的图），调高 `fillerRun`。若误报来自**代码或标记语言**，说明 `CODE_LINE` 的标记集还不够——那是要改代码、而不是调阈值的信号。
- **只输出装饰的流会被兜底判据拦下，阈值可调。** 默认 400 已高于实测最宽合法排版（151），但如果你的场景里合法图形更长，把它调高即可。
- **护栏本身只缓解症状。** 如果你的 provider 支持更低的推理档位，那才是针对病因——可以打开**降低思考强度**开关，或者在你的 DSH 配置里直接调低。

> **AI disclosure** — This project was written with AI assistance: the source code, tests, documentation and commit messages were drafted by an AI agent (DSH Agent, running on DeepSeek Harness) under human direction. The human author defined the requirements, made the design decisions and performed the final review.

Detects and aborts **repeating reasoning** in [DSH](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — the "thinking-loop stall" where a model finishes its actual reasoning and then spins forever on *"about to write the answer"*, burning minutes and hundreds of thousands of characters before the user gives up and hits Stop. It turns a multi-minute silent hang into an immediate, visible error.

In one recorded session (12 turns, 324 steps), **11 of the 12 turns** ended the same way: the model **had already finished the real engineering work** — reading screenshots, computing coordinates, deciding which script to patch — and then stalled on "preparing to output", repeatedly urging itself on without ever writing (`Let me write. Go. OK. Emit. Now.`). A single step emitted **240,000–280,000 characters** over **208 seconds**, ending only when the user pressed Stop. Those 11 assistant messages had an **empty `stopReason`** and **a single `reasoning` block** — no `text`, no `tool-call`: the model never produced one executable action, it was idling inside its own thinking. DSH had no guard that could notice and stop early.

**The approach.** The plugin mounts on the `llm/stream` waterfall (the same extension point DSH's own `llm-invariant` gate uses), **measures only the streaming reasoning text**, and every 200 characters evaluates five criteria over a rolling buffer. The moment one fires it **stops pulling from upstream** and emits a terminating chunk:

```js
{ type: "finish", reason: { kind: "error", failure: { message, code: "REASONING_LOOP_GUARD" } } }
```

DSH then handles it through its existing provider-error path: the step ends with a visible error instead of idling silently. **The result**: all 11 recorded real failures were **caught within 10,000 characters**; across 2,799 real reasoning streams from this machine (19.2 M characters) it fires 7 times, and **every one is a real loop**.

| Rule | Definition | Measured peak (11 positive / 166 negative) | Threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `periodic-run` (primary) | The buffer tail holds ≥ `minUnits` **consecutive identical units** of period p ∈ [8, 400]; a unit that is itself a shorter string repeated is a typed-out pattern, not a loop, and does not count | positives **0..8** units, negatives **0..2** | 4 |
| `block-repeat` | The same `blockMin`-character block occurs ≥ `blockCount` times in the window, **at an equal stride** | positives **0..2**, negatives **0..0** | 4 |
| `line-repeat` | The same **prose** line (≥ `lineMin` characters) occurs ≥ `lineCount` times **and** those repeats occupy ≥ `lineShare` of the window; code, markup and diff rows are measured but never reported | positives **2..2**, negatives **0..0** | 3 + 10% |
| `kgram-repeat` | The last `kgram` characters occur ≥ `kgramThreshold` times in the window | positives **1..5**, negatives **1..1** | 12 |
| `filler-run` (last resort) | The **raw** text ends with ≥ `fillerRun` consecutive decoration characters (whitespace / punctuation / symbols) | see "Decoration is not a loop" below | 400 |

The rules are **disjunctive**: a positive need not trip any particular one, only reach any threshold. Of the 11 recorded failures, **2 were caught by `periodic-run` and 9 by `line-repeat`**; the best ratio across negatives only reaches **0.50** while the lowest positive reaches **1.00**. **Only `reasoning-delta` is measured, never `block-end`** — the latter replays the whole block text, which would manufacture the very repetition being looked for. **`text-delta` is never measured**: ordinary long output (tables, code) can legitimately repeat, and a missed detection is better than a false abort.

> **Co-occurrence inside one window is not a loop.** The three counting rules above originally only asked "how many times did this appear in the window". One real session produced 5 false fires in a row from exactly that mistake: the model citing the same Java statement repeatedly while reasoning, several parallel `runcode` commands sharing a prefix, and a literal block of 36 `x` characters it was genuinely typing out. A loop is a repetition **in time** — advancing at a constant stride, or continuing to the tail. That is why the discriminators now come in layers, below.

"The same line twice" is normal when reasoning while writing code or docs — a refactor puts one identifier on two lines, a changelog draft writes `## Unreleased` twice — and either one aborts the user's stream. The 177-sample calibration set **could not show this**, because its 11 positives and 166 negatives are **all prose** and contain none of the "reasoning while writing code" failure shape: on that shape, `0/166` proves nothing at all.

The real calibration was therefore redone on **2,799 reasoning streams from this machine** (19.2M characters, including the 11 known loops). The old defaults fire **180 times** on that corpus (`line-repeat` 177, `block-repeat` 3); the new defaults fire **7 times, all of them real loops**. What the numbers said:

- **Count alone does not separate.** The commonest healthy tic, `Let me write.`, reaches 17 occurrences while the weakest real loop reaches 29 — only a 1.7× margin, too thin to justify interrupting a user.
- **Share is the discriminator.** Repeats occupy at most **6.1%** of a healthy window and at least **10.2%** of a looping one. 8% lets two false positives through, 12% misses real loops, so the default is 10%.
- **Count cannot go back to 2 either.** A single 72-character **prose** line occurring **twice** already pushes the share to 18.7%, which no share floor can catch. (The original argument used a 41-character identifier, but identifiers are now excluded by the third condition below, so it had to be restated in prose.)
- **`block-repeat` only needed `blockCount` 3 → 4.** At 3 it fires whenever healthy reasoning *quotes long text* (a hex dump, a plugin-name listing, a restatement of the system prompt); at 4 the corpus yields 3 fires, all real loops. No share floor is applied here on purpose — every value from 0% to 25% gives the same answer, so one would be complexity without evidence.

**The third condition: a reported line must not be code.** Normalization strips whitespace, punctuation and symbols — which is exactly the information that distinguishes two lines of code. One real false positive: inside an 801-character reasoning fragment, these five lines

```
if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {                    (an ordinary quotation, three times)
-                if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {   (a diff deletion row)
+                if (e.isKeyboardEvent()) {   (a diff insertion row)
```

all normalize to `ifeisKeyboardEvent`, so "the same line occurs 5 times, occupying 22.6% of the window" crossed both floors at once. The model was not looping — it was reasoning about a code change, and its next attempt was 4,084 characters of ordinary work that trips no rule. The fire also landed in the very first judging window (`minChars`-sized), where a handful of repeats already occupies a large share.

**No threshold could reach it.** `lineCount` would have to go from 3 to 6 to stop this one, and 6 already sits inside the range real loops occupy; pushing `lineShare` past it would cost real detections in the fixtures. So the rule now **does not report** lines that `CODE_LINE` classifies as code, markup or a diff row, but **still counts them in the denominator** (removing them from the denominator too would inflate the share of code-dense streams — the mirror image of the same mistake).

| Candidate fix | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Raise `lineCount` / `lineShare` | Either misses real loops, or merely moves the bar elsewhere |
| Strip diff markers before normalizing | **Ineffective** — `STRIP` already strips `-` / `+` and whitespace, so stripping first changes nothing |
| Drop normalization entirely | **Ineffective** — the same fragment still reaches `count=3 · share=11.3%` and fires |
| **Exclude by line kind** (adopted) | The false positive is gone, and it is a **class** exclusion, not a raised threshold |

Re-checked against **3,862 real reasoning streams from this machine**: the fix removes that fire and one other false positive of the same shape (three quoted `

` lines from HTML) and changes **nothing else** — the fixtures still score 166 healthy with 0 false positives and 11 degenerate all detected, and the corpus's two `line-repeat` fires are the same real loops (`count` 30 and 19, unchanged). The marker set is deliberately narrow — braces, markup tags, a leading diff marker — none of which occur in ordinary prose; a wider rule (excluding any bracket or operator) would also suppress `The config (see above) is wrong.`, blinding the rule to genuine prose tics.

This also fixed a semantic defect: `line-repeat` / `block-repeat` used to return at the first qualifying unit, so the `count` in the journal always equalled the threshold and never reported the real repetition count. Both now scan the whole buffer for the largest repeating unit, so `count` is a true measurement.

readme.section: One window is not a loop: the second layer
readme.text: Five false fires in one session each exposed the same false premise, but needed three different answers:

readme.section: One window is not a loop: the second layer
readme.text:
| What happened | What the old rule saw | What was really going on | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The same Java statement cited four times (`StarSystemAPI sys = (StarSystemAPI)Global…getContainingLocation();`) | `line-repeat`: `count=4`, `share=10.2%`, just over both floors | Four citations spread across the window at gaps of **424 / 602 / 259** — no rhythm at all | Recognize the line as code: `CODE_LINE` gains a **trailing semicolon** and a **dotted call chain** |
| Four parallel `runcode` commands (add planet / asteroid belt / nebula / ring) sharing the prefix that reads the current system | `block-repeat`: the same 100-character block 4 times | Gaps of **1130 / 359 / 742** — parallel commands, not a loop | Require repeats **at an equal stride** (`count` now reports the longest equal-stride chain; the raw occurrence count survives as `rawCount`) |
| The model writing a 6×6 tile literal `"xxxxxxxx…"` | `periodic-run`: `units=4`, `period=8` | The unit `xxxxxxxx` is itself **one character repeated** — it was typing, not looping | Reject a unit that is itself an integer repeat of a shorter string (`isRepeatedUnit`) |

readme.section: One window is not a loop: the second layer
readme.text: All three are **class judgments**, not raised thresholds. Raising thresholds had already been ruled out by measurement: `lineCount` would have to go from 3 to 6 to stop the first case, and 6 already sits inside the range real loops occupy.

readme.section: One window is not a loop: the second layer
readme.text: Verification: on the same corpus, run at chunk sizes 7 / 41 / 200, the fire set is **byte-identical before and after** the three changes (the two `line-repeat` fires at `count` 29 / 19 and the two `periodic-run` fires), the fixtures still score 166 healthy with 0 false positives and 11 degenerate all detected, and all five false fires turn inert.

readme.section: Why the text is normalized first
readme.text: The first four rules count on the **normalized** text: whitespace, punctuation and symbols are stripped before anything is measured. That is not cosmetic — it fixes a real false positive. The original implementation ran the periodic rule on the raw buffer, so a model drawing a `________` rule became "8 characters repeated 6 times", the guard really did abort that stream, and the journal kept a record with an eight-underscore preview.

readme.section: Why the text is normalized first
readme.text: The strip class is `[\s\p{P}\p{S}]`. It is a **strict superset** of the hand-written list it replaced: `_` is `\p{Pc}` (connector punctuation) and `─` / `▁` are `\p{So}`, both of which the old list missed. On all 11 real degenerate blobs the two classes produce **byte-identical output** — so widening it removed decoration only, never a character any real loop depended on.

readme.section: Decoration is not a loop, but drawing decoration forever is
readme.text: Normalization costs one thing: a stream emitting **nothing but** decoration leaves the four counting rules with an empty text. `filler-run` exists for exactly that case, and is deliberately dull:

readme.section: Decoration is not a loop, but drawing decoration forever is
readme.text:
- **It is anchored to the end of the text.** A model may legitimately draw a wide table or an ASCII diagram; once it moves on to prose the decoration is no longer at the tail and stops counting. Only an *ongoing* decoration stream can fire — scanning the whole window would fire on any diagram the model had already finished.
- **The bar sits far above legitimate formatting.** Measured over real shapes, the longest decoration run is **151** characters (a 150-wide ASCII box), then **142** (a 20-column markdown table row), **62** (a setext underline), **5** (a `---` rule); the false positive that motivated the rule was only **8** underscores. The default 400 is 2.6× the widest legitimate shape found, and a genuinely stuck stream crosses it within one `every` interval.

readme.section: Decoration is not a loop, but drawing decoration forever is
readme.text: Across six feeding granularities (chunk = 1 / 8 / 40 / 200 / 1000 / 4000) the five rules still score **11/11 detections and 0/166 false positives**.

`validateConfig()` rejects configurations that would **silently fail to work** — `kgram > window`, `minPeriod >= maxPeriod`, `periodTail < 2 * maxPeriod`, an empty `failureCode`, a non-positive `every`, and so on — with a message naming the offending field.

The `enabled`, `settingsPath` and seven switch fields above are also editable **in the GUI** — except `settingsPath`, which is set only in the patch and merely shown **read-only**. Open this plugin on the Plugins page and, below the trigger-log panel, the detail view gains six blocks — **loop guard** (the core switch), **automatic recovery**, **lower reasoning effort**, **strip past thinking**, **notify on abort**, and a read-only **config file** path. Save and the values are written to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-reasoning-loop-guard/config.json`.

**The core guard and the abort notice default to on; the three arms default to off.** The core switch *is* the plugin; the notice only puts a line on screen and changes nothing sent to the provider, so it is on too. The three arms each change behaviour beyond the guard itself, so the default takes the conservative side. **Turn the core guard off and the three arms go inert with it**: they can only ever react to a failure the guard itself raised, and once the guard watches no stream it raises none.

**The core switch is not the same thing as the patch key of the same name, but the two never fight.** `enabled: false` in the patch means "register no hooks at all"; it is read once at load. The `enabled` in the settings file is read **per request** by the stream listener. The test is "**only an explicit `false` turns it off**": a missing key means "as shipped", i.e. on — so an older `config.json` can never be misread as a shutdown. **Saving needs no restart**: `config.json` overrides the patch **key by key**, and every read folds again, so the change takes effect on the next request. Writes are atomic (temp file + rename), and the read side falls back to the baseline on a missing or malformed `config.json` and **never throws** — the worst a broken settings file can do is send the switches back to their defaults, never make the guard inactive. **The GUI can write those eight keys and nothing else; detection thresholds always stay in the patch**, so "which file did this fire's threshold come from?" never becomes a question you have to guess at.

- **Automatic recovery** (`recovery.*`). After the guard aborts a stream, it appends a corrective message to the session and retries the same step. **Why the message has to come first**: a retry re-sends **the identical request** (`buildRequest` re-derives messages from the session log, and the aborted `assistant/attempt` does not take part), so a bare retry with no new message necessarily reproduces the same loop. The retry budget is counted **per step** (`sessionId:turn:step`) — per session would disable the arm forever after one bad turn, per attempt would make `maxRetries` meaningless. The message carries the **producer's own `source.kind`** (session format v4 rejects `kind: "plugin"`), which has the side effect that the chat UI renders it as a context note rather than a user bubble. Any internal failure in this arm falls through to `next()`, so a failure stays as terminal as it would be without the plugin.

**`failureCode` deliberately sits outside the default retryable set.** The retryable codes are `EMPTY_RESPONSE / RATE_LIMIT / SERVER / TIMEOUT / TRANSPORT`; `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` is not among them, so `dsh-llm-retry` will not retry automatically. The reason: repetition is a property of the *request itself*, so an automatic retry re-sends the whole prompt and burns the same tokens to loop again. If you do want retries, set `failureCode: EMPTY_RESPONSE`.

**`failureCode` is namespaced by default so it cannot cross-talk with another plugin.** Before 0.2.0 the default was the generic `REASONING_LOOP`, and **other plugins ship their own loop detection and drive their own recovery off the failure code**. One real collision measured on this machine: `dsh-our-free-model` v2.0.0 bundles its own `loop-recovery` in `vendor/channel-pack/pack.js`, and it matches `error.code === "REASONING_LOOP"` exactly to decide whether to **auto-resume** — so this guard's aborts were captured as that plugin's own failures, and it responded by calling `agent.followup()` with a message stamped `source.kind: "user"` to queue a whole new turn. Two consequences, both hard to trace: **(1)** with all three of this plugin's switches off, it still looked like it "fired automatically", because the resume did not come from this plugin at all; **(2)** pressing the stop button did not stop it — the button only aborts the current stream, while the already-queued resume message runs anyway. With `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` the exact match no longer hits.

**This cross-talk cannot be rooted out in principle.** The namespace only blocks third-party recovery that matches the generic code **exactly**. If some plugin switches to a prefix match, or also claims `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD`, the collision is back — and the only remaining move is to set `failureCode` to a value neither side claims. Note the reverse direction too: **a loop that another plugin detects on its own still takes that plugin's recovery path**, and this plugin's switches cannot reach it.

**Emergency stopgap: environment variables.** If "every switch is off yet it resumed by itself, and Stop would not stop it" happens again, you can shut down the third party's half with environment variables instead of waiting for a new release of this plugin:

| Variable | Set to | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DSH_REASONING_LOOP_GUARD` | `0` | Turns off the third-party plugin's **own** loop detection. |
| `DSH_REASONING_LOOP_AUTO_RESUME` | `0` | Turns off the third-party plugin's **automatic resume**. |

Both are read by that plugin as "**on unless set**" (it only treats `0` / `false` / `no` / `off` as off), so you must set them to `0` explicitly. **They only affect that plugin's own behaviour, not this guard** — this plugin reads no `DSH_*` environment variable. Set them as **system/user environment variables**, not in `~/.dsh/.env`: DSH's launcher reserves the `DSH_` prefix as "settable only by the launching environment", so a value written to `.env` is rejected outright.

```powershell

readme.section: environment blocks by explorer.exe at sign-in, and existing processes never receive the later write.
readme.text:
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('DSH_REASONING_LOOP_GUARD', '0', 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('DSH_REASONING_LOOP_AUTO_RESUME', '0', 'User')
```

**A fresh detector per stream.** An automatic retry starts counting from zero, so a previous attempt's repetition never accumulates into the next one.

During development the guard was additionally verified end to end against the **real `dsh` CLI driving a real agent loop**, on an isolated profile whose default model was a test-only adapter replaying a degenerate reasoning stream — two arms, eleven assertions: with the guard armed the exit code is **1**, upstream actually emitted only **3120 / 7659 chars**, and stderr carries `REASONING_LOOP_GUARD: …`; with the guard off the same stream runs to completion with exit code **0**, **7659 / 7659 chars**, printing `TG-FAKE-OK` on stdout. That is: the guard **really did cut the upstream generator short**, while with the guard off the identical stream completed untouched — ruling out a broken test rig. The end-to-end harness is development scaffolding and is not part of the published package.

The guard's thresholds were calibrated against a real failure, but that session's reasoning text is private, so the committed fixtures in [`test/fixtures/`](test/fixtures/) are **synthetic**. They reproduce the *measured shape* of the original data — the same row counts (11 / 166), the same per-row character counts (a 244k-character blob, down to 502 characters), and the same loop geometry. The generator is seeded and deterministic, so regenerating reproduces byte-identical files and any diff is a real change.

- **Not a general-purpose watchdog.** The rules target one specific degenerate shape — contiguous repetition at the tail. A different kind of stall (an infinite tool-call loop, or a model circling semantically without repeating itself literally) will not trigger it.
- **Where it first fires** depends on feeding granularity: as early as ~3000 characters, as late as ~56000. All eleven recorded failures would have been caught within 10,000 characters.
- **The original calibration was 177 samples from a single session — and it has a known blind spot.** All of them are prose and none of them is the "reasoning while writing code" shape, so the `0/166` measured there **cannot** be extrapolated. The `line-repeat` / `block-repeat` thresholds were later recalibrated on thousands of real streams (see "Why `line-repeat` needs three conditions").
